newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thai vehicle sales seen on target despite economy.
newsitem.headline: Thai vehicle sales seen on target despite economy.

text.p: Thailand's vehicle sales should meet projected targets in 1996 despite the country's sluggish economic growth, an industry spokeman said on Tuesday.
"It is possible that 165,000 more units will be sold in the remaining three months," Surapong Pasitpanapong, spokesman for the Thai Automobile Industry Association, told Reuters.

"Although the sales of passenger cars and one-tonne pick up trucks have been affected by the sluggish economy, the demand for commercial vehicles during the harvest season will offset that," he added.

In the first nine months of the year, total passenger cars and vehicle sales in Thailand were up 5.2 percent to 435,021 units compared with 413,684 in the same period last year, according to data provided by Toyota Motor (Thailand).
The automobile association has projected the number of vehicles sold in Thailand would reach 600,000-610,000 units this year against 570,000 in 1995.
Surapong said the slowing economy significantly affected vehicle sales during January to September.
"But the sales in the first nine months were still higher than in the same period last year because there were a lot of new models being launched in the period," the spokesman said.
"If the economy is good, the sales would show a double digit growth with several new models being launched," he added.
Surapong expect vehicle sales in Thailand next year to be around the same level as this year because no new models are due to be launched.
